title: Developer Experience Docs Site: Operating Procedures & Canonical Content Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:
This page defines the operating procedures, content standards, and common playbooks for maintaining Redwood Inference's developer-facing documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs site operations, and the canonical 'top support issues' + fixes list. Use this playbook for authoring, reviewing, publishing, incident handling, and periodic audits of developer docs.

Goals:
- Ensure documentation is accurate, discoverable, and production-grade for engineers integrating Redwood APIs and SDKs.
- Maintain a single source of truth for canonical fixes to top support issues.
- Provide reliable ops runbooks for the docs site build, deploy, and incident recovery.

Scope:
Applies to all content under eng-developer-experience: sdk-guides, quickstarts-and-templates, api-examples, docs-site, and support-top-issues.

Owner & RACI:
- Document Owner: Developer Experience (DevEx) Docs team (primary: Asha Patel).
- Reviewers: SDK maintainers, Platform/Runtime engineers, Support triage lead.
- RACI summary:
  - Responsible: Docs author (creates PR), DevEx editors (review + merge).
  - Accountable: Head of Developer Experience (approves major changes).
  - Consulted: SDK owners, Security, Legal (for restricted content).
  - Informed: Developer community, Customer Success.

Content & Formatting Standards (must-follow):
1) Metadata: every page must include front-matter metadata and match Confluence metadata policy (title, space, author, owner_team, status, created_at, last_updated). Use ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD).
2) File naming: short, descriptive, hyphen-separated, include year only for high-level playbooks or stable templates (example: developer-experience-docs-site-operating-procedures-2026.json).
3) Language & tone: concise, second-person imperative for procedures, present-tense descriptive for references. Avoid personal notes.
4) Structure: intro paragraph, quick summary bullets, sections with headings, numbered procedures for runbooks, and a 'Related resources' section.
5) Code & examples: provide copy-paste snippets, include expected outputs. Use fenced code blocks and include CLI path for local builds.
6) Tables: use pipe-delimited tables for configuration matrices, SLOs, and ownership matrices.

Canonical Content Types & Templates (quick reference):
- SDK Guide: Purpose, Installation, Quick example, Full API reference links, Versioning & changelog, Troubleshooting, Tests & CI snippet.
- Quickstart/Template: Problem statement, Expected outcome, Minimal working example, Deploy/run steps, Common errors, Links to prebuilt repo/template.
- API Example: Single-responsibility snippet, Input/Output example, Rate-limit considerations, Parameter description table, SDK + curl variants.
- Support Top Issue: Issue summary, Root cause analysis, Canonical steps to reproduce, Fix/mitigation, Postmortem links if applicable.

Authoring workflow (step-by-step):
1) Create or update the document in the canonical repo (see docs-site README). Start from the closest template in quickstarts-and-templates.
2) Add required metadata at the top of the JSON doc. Ensure created_at & last_updated are set.
3) Run local validation: schema-lint, spellcheck, and link-checker.
   - Commands: 
     ```bash
     make docs-validate
     mkdocs build --strict 
     ./scripts/link-checker ./site/_site || true
     ```
4) Open a PR to the docs repo with a clear description and list of reviewers (add SDK owner + support lead).
5) Review checklist (for reviewers):
   - Does code run as advertised? (execute quickstart)
   - Are SLOs, thresholds and ownership included where relevant?
   - Is there a canonical support-fix entry for any new error class?
   - Security review (if the doc includes credential handling or private deployment steps).
6) Merge after at least one domain owner approval and DevEx editor sign-off. For breaking changes or deprecations, schedule a coordinated release (see Release cadence).

Release cadence & notifications:
- Minor content updates: merged to main and deployed automatically. Post PR merge: add Slack notif to #devex-docs with summary.
- Major updates (SDK behavior changes, breaking API examples): schedule a content freeze window and coordinate with SDK owners. Send an announcement via internal dev-ex and customer-success channels.

Versioning & Deprecation policy:
- All SDK guides and API examples must include the supported version range. When deprecating an example or call pattern, add a prominent deprecation banner and migration steps. Deprecation timeline minimum: 90 days.

Docs Site Operations (runbook & critical procedures):
- Platform: internal MkDocs-based site, CI builds via GitHub Actions, static hosting via internal CDN + Varnish.
- SLOs: docs site uptime 99.9% monthly; search index freshness <= 15 min after a merge.

Runbook: Build failure (triage):
1) Symptoms: site build fails in CI; preview deploy fails; link-checker errors.
2) Immediate check: open last CI run, capture error logs.
3) If error is transient (network timeout, package registry): re-run job.
4) If error is content-related (broken link, malformed front-matter): revert the offending PR, notify author, and patch.
5) Escalation: if >30 min to restore preview or build repeatedly fails, create incident in PagerDuty and follow the oncall incident playbook.

Runbook: Search index rebuild (manual):
1) Trigger: a large metadata change or search anomalies.
2) Command: 
   ```bash
   ./scripts/reindex-search --env=prod 
   tail -f /var/log/docs-search.log # monitor progress
   ```
3) Expected duration: 5-20 minutes. If >30 min, open an ops ticket (eng-platform).

Top Support Issues: triage + canonical fixes
- Maintain a living `support-top-issues` page with the top 20 recurring issues. Each entry must include: symptom, most-likely causes, reproduction steps, short fix, long-term remediation, and owner.
- Example entry: 
  Title: 401 Unauthorized when using API key from Dedicated instance
  Symptom: API returns 401 for valid key in Dedicated.
  Reproduction: call POST /v1/generate with header Authorization: Bearer <key>.
  Root cause: customer used global hosted key against a Dedicated endpoint.
  Canonical fix: verify endpoint host, use dedicated key from console or rotate key. Link to console doc.
  Owner: Customer Success - Dedicated accounts.

Support Flow & Escalation for doc-related bugs:
1) Support engineer files a request in the docs repo with label `docs-bug` and provides reproduction and suggested docs patch.
2) DevEx triage: evaluate, prioritize (P0–P3), and assign to author or editor.
3) For P0 (broken quickstart, incorrect security guidance): patch + hotfix release, notify #support and #devex-docs, update the top-issues page.

Analytics & quality signals:
- Track: pageviews, time-on-page, search queries with zero results, number of support tickets referencing a doc page, and quickstart run success rate (via telemetry from sample repos).
- Quarterly audit: pages with < 50 views and high bounce rates are reviewed for consolidation or archival.

A checklist for publishing a new Quickstart (template):
- [ ] Uses official template from quickstarts-and-templates folder
- [ ] Includes one-line summary and expected output screenshot or sample log
- [ ] Has copy-paste runnable commands (curl + SDK)
- [ ] Includes permissions/KMS notes if credentials are used
- [ ] Tests included in CI that run the quickstart at least once/month
- [ ] Linked to matching API example and SDK guide

Example configuration table (ownership & SLOs):
| Area | Owner | SLO | Review cadence | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Docs site build | DevEx (Asha Patel) | 99.9% uptime | Daily CI checks | Alerts to #devex-ops |
| SDK examples | SDK owners | Example correctness 100% | Weekly | Automate smoke tests |
| Support-top-issues | Support lead | Pages updated within 3 business days for P0/P1 | Continuous | Link to incident tickets |

Security & legal reviews:
- Any content that describes customer data controls, private deployment, or includes customer-owned config must be labeled `restricted` and routed to Security + Legal reviewers.
- Do not embed secrets or long-lived tokens in examples. Use placeholders and recommend ephemeral credentials.

Maintenance & audit schedule:
- Weekly: triage PR backlog and high-priority support-fixes.
- Monthly: run link-checker, spellcheck, and test quickstarts.
- Quarterly: full content audit (remove stale pages, reconcile versioning).
- Annual: update top-issues list and run a simulated support drill for the top 5 recurring issues.

Appendix: Useful commands & CI snippets
- Local preview:
  ```bash
  mkdocs serve -f mkdocs.yml
  # Visit http://localhost:8000 to validate locally
  ```
- CI validate (GitHub Actions snippet):
  ```yaml
  jobs:
    validate-docs:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        - run: make docs-validate
        - run: mkdocs build --strict
        - run: ./scripts/link-checker ./site/_site || true
  ```

Related resources:
- Quickstarts & templates folder (internal): confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates
- SDK guides: confluence/eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides
- Support top issues: confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues
- Docs site repo README: github.redwood/internal/docs-site

Contact & escalation:
- Primary doc owner: Asha Patel (DevEx) — asha.patel@redwoodinference.internal
- Support triage lead: Marcus Li — marcus.li@redwoodinference.internal
- On-call: follow standard oncall roster (eng-oncall) for platform incidents.
